date_note: The page gives no earlier day for the attack; the East-West Center emailed participants and alumni on 9 and 18 November, and the Honolulu Star-Advertiser report is dated 24 November.
title: East-West Center says its participant registration database was targeted in a cyberattack
geo_basis: East-West Center in Manoa, Honolulu, as the article states
summary: The East-West Center in Manoa says a cyberattack targeted its participant registration database, which holds records of anyone who ever registered with the center. According to the Honolulu Star-Advertiser, the database remains offline and the incident remains under investigation. The center says it has no evidence the data compromise resulted in actual misuse of personal records, and it is paying for two years of credit monitoring.
plain: The East-West Center says its database of people who registered with it was attacked. It is offline and under investigation. The center says it has no evidence of misuse and offers two years of free credit monitoring.
exec: A cyberattack hit the East-West Center's participant registration database; the center says it has no evidence of misuse and is offering credit monitoring.
action: The East-West Center says enrolling in its two years of Experian IdentityWorks credit monitoring is highly recommended; the FBI recommends reporting cyber intrusions at ic3.gov.

validation.note: One publisher read (Honolulu Star-Advertiser, republished by The Garden Island), quoting the center's own statement. The center gave no count of people affected and no data types; it did not answer questions on reporting to the FBI or on ransom demands. The article does not link the attack to any tool or actor.

review.note: compared title, date, statement, credit monitoring and FBI advice with the article
